title: feat(plugin-auth): the SSO Providers form sets, shows and clears the groups claim
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9VJA5ftzZj6fH6CEjFbETUE)_

Fixes #31666

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Setup → SSO Providers 表单现在能设置、查看和清除 SSO 组声明（groups claim），写入的位置与 `/sso/register` 完全相同：`mapping.extraFields.groups`。
- 为什么改：#31657 之后登录会按 IdP 组授予权限集，但组声明只能经 API 配置，管理员在界面上无法完成这一步。
- 风险与回滚：只新增两个仅限平台管理员的动作和两个注册参数；另修了一个现存缺陷（带 `oidcConfig` 的 update-provider 对密钥存于 `sys_secret` 的 OIDC 提供方一律返回 400）。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts` 末尾的两个桥，以及 `objectql-adapter.ts` 里 `update` 回显的密钥注入。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts src/register-sso-provider.test.ts src/admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts`。
- 需要你做的：无；两个新路由名由席位裁定（见下）。

## What changes

The Setup → SSO Providers form is metadata (`sys_sso_provider` actions with flat params that post to plugin-auth `/admin/sso/*` bridges), not console code, so the whole change sits in plugin-auth and platform-objects. Nothing under `ui/` or `packages/spec/**` changes.

- **Register SSO Provider** gains **Map: Groups claim** and **Register SAML Provider** gains **Map: Groups attribute**. A non-blank value lands on `mapping.extraFields.groups`, exactly where `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/register` stores it. Blank stores no `extraFields`, as today.
- **Show Groups Claim** posts to the new `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/get-groups-claim`, which reads the stored row (system read, `oidc_config` / `saml_config` recovered) and answers only `{ providerId, groupsClaim }`.
- **Edit Groups Claim** posts to the new `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/set-groups-claim`. It merges the claim into the stored mapping (every other member kept verbatim), writes through the vendor's own `/sso/update-provider`, and reads the claim back. A blank claim deletes `extraFields.groups` (and an emptied `extraFields`), so the provider signs users in exactly like one saved without it.
- Both routes run `gateAdmin` first, the platform-admin gate of the other `/admin/sso` bridges. A refused vendor update answers its status with the standard code for it and a fixed sentence; the vendor's body is never relayed, so no other config member (client secret, certificate, endpoints, other mapping members) can reach an answer.
- **Fix:** `@better-auth/sso` reads the provider for `/sso/update-provider` through `lockSSOProviderRow`, which is an adapter `update`. That echo did not run the read half (`injectClientSecretOnRead`), so any update-provider carrying an `oidcConfig` for a provider whose secret is held in `sys_secret` was refused 400 "clientSecret is required". The adapter's `update` now carries the secret and the IdP-initiated column into its echo like every other provider read.
- Two route-ledger rows, two platform-objects affordance rows, docs page `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` updated, translations for ten locales.
- The #31657 grant logic (`sso-group-projection.ts`) is untouched.

New public route names (`/admin/sso/get-groups-claim`, `/admin/sso/set-groups-claim`) and action names (`show_sso_groups_claim`, `edit_sso_groups_claim`) follow the `/admin/sso/*` and `*_sso_*` house spelling; they are the seat's call. No new error code: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR / INVALID_REQUEST, 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 401/403 from the existing gate.

## Why

Since #31657 an SSO sign-in grants the permission sets mapped to the provider's IdP groups, read from `mapping.extraFields.groups`. Only the vendor register API could set that member (documented by #31664); an administrator working in Setup had no way to configure it.

## Verification

Clause-② measured: on base `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/set-groups-claim` and `get-groups-claim` are not mounted and the register forms carry no groups param; on head both routes answer a platform admin 200 and the register forms accept the new param. A widening only: no request accepted on main is now refused.

Tests (all import `src`):

- `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts`, new describe: a form save with a claim stores the register door's mapping and the next sign-in grants the mapped set (the #31657 pin shape). CONTROL: a blank claim writes nothing and grants nothing. CONTROL: Show on a register-door row answers `groups`, then a clear removes it. Round trip on a rich mapping (register-door row and a row this action changed): every other member kept verbatim.
- `register-sso-provider.test.ts`: both register forms store the claim where the register door does (compared to a direct `/sso/register` row), CONTROL without it; the bridges' merge, clear, 404 and 400; a no-leak pin (client secret, certificate, client id, IdP URL, other mapping members never appear in any answer, including a vendor refusal carrying them; data keys are exactly `providerId` and `groupsClaim`).
- `admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts`: for both routes, anonymous 401 and member / org-admin / position-named-admin 403 with neither the store read nor the vendor called; platform admin 200.
- `sso-client-secret-at-rest.test.ts` ③b: an update-provider carrying only `oidcConfig.mapping` is accepted and the secret still reads back.

Ablations (each restored, `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards):

- Gate removed from set-groups-claim → 4 gate tests red (`expected 200 to be 401` / `403`).
- Vendor refusal body relayed → the no-leak test red.
- Mapping added to the show answer → 2 tests red (data had 3 keys, expected 2).
- Echo injection removed from the adapter `update` → ③b and the round trip red (`clientSecret is required …`, 400).

Runs: plugin-auth full suite 4431 passed, 10 skipped, 1 red (the route-ledger pin, which hand-lists the mounts); that file re-run green (10/10) after the pin named the two routes; platform-objects 120 files / 1933 tests green; typecheck green for both packages; lint (`eslint --no-inline-config`) clean on both packages; `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:auth-mount-ledger` OK; every `dispatch-gates --commands` command run and reconciled with `--ran`. Dogfood, run locally under the verify lock after the sweep fix: the whole `@objectstack/dogfood` package 440 files passed, 3 skipped; 3653 tests passed, 41 skipped; 0 failed. The five admin suites together 5/5 files, 34/34 tests. Control: without the new entries the non-admin sweep is red at `:618` with the queue's signature.

Forced test edits (existing tests changed because the surface grew):

- `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts`: `bootGroupEngine` now registers the auth object extensions and `sys_secret` and sets a fake crypto provider, so the harness holds a client secret the way production does.
- `platform-objects.test.ts`: two rows in the action table (`show_sso_groups_claim`, `edit_sso_groups_claim`).
- `platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts`: the same two actions on the floor list.
- `auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: the hand-written objectstack-mount pin names the two new routes.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts`: the two routes join `ADMITTED` (ADR-0068 gate first) with probe bodies; the admin reaches the handler and gets 404 for the unknown probe provider, nothing moves.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`: the two routes join the `objectstack-gate` bucket with the same probe bodies (anonymous 401, member 403; admin measured 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND).

Both dogfood sweeps derive the served `/admin/` route set and refuse an unclassified mount; PR CI does not run the dogfood shards, so the merge queue caught them (run 42562448270, Dogfood 3/3; then Dogfood 1/3). Census of `packages/qa/dogfood/test`: only these two files derive the `/admin/` set. `admin-credential-lifecycle`, `admin-identity-audit-trail` and `admin-ledger-decision-metadata` name fixed routes and need no registration.

Out of scope, noted: ADR-0011's "Not assessed" list could name the two new actions (governed surface, left alone); the cloud auth proxy must mount the two new routes to serve them there.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English. (The `## 维护者速读` section is Chinese by the dispatch order.)
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
